linkedin.hook: Isolated SmartAccount architecture solves the contagion problem in decentralized lending pools.
linkedin.copy:
Shared collateral models present an unpriced externality for institutional capital on Soroban. When a volatile asset degrades within a lending pool, cross-margined participants subsidize bad debt through haircut mechanisms or liquidation cascades. Blend v2 addresses pool-level risk through formal verification, yet client execution still requires deterministic boundaries to protect automated yield strategies.

Vanna handles this through dedicated SmartAccount execution sandboxes. Instead of commingling positions, margin credit routes programmatically into Blend v2 b-tokens with strict state isolation. The underlying risk engine enforces a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor, running telemetry via Mercury indexers at ~320ms latency. At 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per invocation, risk checks run atomically without the latency overhead common to EVM rollups.

The result is credit access that restricts downside to individual contract boundaries. Capital allocators can scale yield strategies knowing liquidation mechanics run deterministically at the account layer rather than threatening core protocol solvency. Testnet verification is live for infrastructure developers at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Deep dive: Routing isolated margin credit into Blend v2 b-tokens using Soroban SmartAccounts
reddit.copy:
Cross-margin lending has always forced an uncomfortable compromise between capital efficiency and systemic risk. If you farm on Soroban, you know Blend v2 brings formally verified pools and b-token mechanics to Stellar. The missing component has been deploying levered credit without exposing your broader balance sheet to pool-level contagion.

### Contract Isolation

Instead of borrowing through an externally owned account, user positions deploy inside isolated Soroban smart contracts. Margin credit drawn from Vanna liquidity routes directly into target Blend v2 b-token contracts. Collateral remains constrained within the SmartAccount boundary, ensuring a liquidation in one asset pool cannot touch your positions in another.

### Execution and Settlement Latency

We enforce a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor across every active credit line. Position telemetry runs through Mercury indexers delivering ~320ms latency. Because Stellar locks base execution fees at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas, automated liquidation routines run frequent, granular solvency checks. When an account breaches threshold limits, partial unwinds clear only the necessary b-token balance to restore target margins, preventing sudden total liquidations.

### Verification and Testnet Setup

The b-token wrapper abstracts standard mint and burn calls into atomic Soroban contract invocations. You borrow, supply to the Blend v2 pool, and lock receipt tokens inside your SmartAccount sandbox in a single transaction payload.

You can test the contract interactions and run the sandbox deployment scripts on testnet at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Disclosure: I am an engineer at Vanna Protocol building credit primitives on Soroban. Happy to answer technical questions about state isolation or our indexer pipeline in the comments.
